quarantine.title: Quarantine
quarantine.sub: Mail that looks like spam or is dangerous is held here. Release what is good, block what is not; the spam filter learns from every choice.
quarantine.empty: Quarantine is empty. Nothing is waiting for you.
quarantine.teach_hint: Releasing teaches "this is good mail", blocking teaches "this is spam".
quarantine.released: Released; the message is being delivered.
quarantine.learned: The spam filter learned from it.
quarantine.content_hint: Shown as plain text: links and images are not loaded, so viewing is safe.
quarantine.virus_warning: This message contains a virus. Only an administrator can release it.
quarantine.virus_warning_admin: This message contains a virus. Only release it if you are sure it is a false alarm.

symbols.R_SPF_FAIL: Sending server not allowed by SPF
symbols.DBL_SPAM: Link to a known spam domain

dns.title: DNS toolbox
dns.sub: Check a domain's mail DNS, generate SPF and DMARC, publish straight to Cloudflare and switch domains over to Mailfilter.
dns.not_managed: {{domain}} is not a domain in Mailfilter yet, so going live is not possible. Add it under Domains first.

publish_help.spf: Your current SPF value stays as it is; Mailfilter only adds itself. Nothing else changes.
publish_help.spf_value: This replaces the domain's SPF record with the generated value.
publish_help.dkim: Publishes the public key Mailfilter signs outbound mail with.
publish_help.dmarc: This sets the domain's DMARC record to the value shown.
publish_help.server_spf: The shared record that lists all Mailfilter addresses. Domains include this name.
publish_help.mx: Cloudflare will get exactly these MX records. New records are added before old ones are removed, so mail keeps flowing. You can undo this in the change log.
publish_help.mta_sts: mta-sts.<domain> points to Mailfilter, which serves the policy file. The TXT record tells senders which policy version is current.
publish_help.tls_rpt: Senders that have trouble setting up an encrypted connection send a daily report to this address.
publish_help.tlsa: The TLSA record holds the fingerprint of Mailfilter's key. Certificate renewals keep the same key, so the record stays valid.

problem.waiting_for_dns: Cloudflare already has this record. DNS servers can take up to 30 minutes to show it; nothing more to do.
problem.syntax: The record has a syntax error.
problem.multiple_spf: The domain has more than one SPF record; receivers treat that as an error. Remove all but one.
problem.no_all: The record has no "all" at the end.
problem.plus_all: "+all" allows the whole internet to send for this domain.
problem.ptr_deprecated: The "ptr" mechanism is deprecated and slow.
problem.long: The record is very long; consider an include.
problem.mailfilter_missing: Mailfilter is not in the SPF record yet, so outbound mail through Mailfilter may fail SPF.
problem.too_many_lookups: More than 10 DNS lookups: SPF fails at receivers.
problem.too_many_void_lookups: More than 2 lookups that find nothing.
problem.policy_none: Policy "none" only monitors; spoofed mail is still delivered.
problem.pct_partial: The policy applies to only part of the mail.
problem.mismatch: The DNS record does not match the key in Mailfilter.
problem.revoked: The key in DNS is revoked (empty p=).
problem.no_key: Mailfilter has no DKIM key for this domain.
problem.mx_mixed: MX points partly to Mailfilter and partly elsewhere.
problem.mx_elsewhere: MX does not point to Mailfilter yet.
problem.ptr: No matching PTR record for {{value}}. Ask your hosting provider to set it to the Mailfilter host name.
problem.mode_testing: Policy is in test mode: senders report problems but still deliver without encryption.
problem.mode_none: Policy mode is "none": MTA-STS is switched off.
problem.mx_not_in_policy: MX {{value}} is not listed in the policy.
problem.policy_unreachable: The policy file could not be fetched: {{value}}
problem.policy_invalid: The policy file is not a valid MTA-STS policy.
problem.dnssec_off: {{value}} is not signed with DNSSEC, so DANE does not count.
problem.tlsa_mismatch: The published TLSA record does not match Mailfilter's current key.
problem.no_local_cert: No certificate found on this server yet.

note.null_mx: The domain says it accepts no mail at all (null MX).
note.no_mx: No MX record; mail goes to the A/AAAA record of {{host}}.
note.no_address: {{host}} has no IPv4 or IPv6 address.
note.no_starttls: {{host}} has no STARTTLS. Mail to it travels unencrypted.
note.cert_name: The certificate of {{host}} is for another name.

mx.help: Look up where mail for any domain goes, for example a customer's: addresses, reverse DNS, port 25 and STARTTLS.
mx.ph: Any domain, for example a customer's
mx.probe: Also test port 25 and STARTTLS (takes a few seconds)
mx.null_mx: This domain accepts no mail (null MX).

spf.help: Build an SPF record and publish it straight to Cloudflare.
spf.merge_title: Add Mailfilter to an existing SPF
spf.merge_help: Use Check domain and "Publish to Cloudflare" next to SPF: your current value stays and Mailfilter only adds itself.

dmarc.help: Build a DMARC record. Start with "none" to collect reports, then move to quarantine and reject.
dmarc.policy_none: Receivers deliver everything and send you reports.
dmarc.policy_quarantine: Mail that fails goes to the receiver's spam folder.

bl.help: Mailfilter checks its own IPv4 and IPv6 addresses against the major blocklists every 15 minutes.
bl.none_yet: No check has run yet. Click "Check now".
bl.unusable: These lists did not answer their own test entry from this server, so their result is not known: {{lists}}.

cf.title: Cloudflare connection
cf.help: With an API token Mailfilter can publish SPF, DKIM and DMARC and switch MX records for you. Every change is shown first and can be undone.
cf.token_hint: In Cloudflare: My Profile > API Tokens, or Manage Account > API Tokens, then Create Token (template "Edit zone DNS" works). Permissions: Zone: Read and DNS: Edit, for the zones Mailfilter may change. No account ID needed: Mailfilter finds it itself. Stored encrypted.
cf.remove_confirm: Remove the Cloudflare token from Mailfilter?
cf.server_spf_help: Publishes {{name}} with all addresses of this server. Domains only include this name, so adding a server later changes one record.

gl.title: Go live
gl.help: One-time switch for this domain: points the MX record in Cloudflare to {{host}}. Mailfilter checks everything first and keeps the old value so you can roll back.

c.accepts: Mailfilter accepts mail for this domain

gl.force: Go live anyway, even though checks failed
gl.done_toast: Live: MX now points to Mailfilter
gl.rollback_confirm: Put the previous MX records back? Mail will go to the old server again.
gl.rolled_back: Rolled back: the previous MX records are back
gl.was_rolled_back: This domain was rolled back earlier. You can go live again.

log.help: Every change Mailfilter made in Cloudflare, with the old value. Undo puts the old value back. Go-live is undone with Roll back on the domain.
log.undo_confirm: Put the old value back in Cloudflare?

alert.title: Mailfilter is on a blocklist
alert.detail: {{ip}} is listed on {{name}} ({{zone}}) since {{time}}. Outbound mail to some providers may be refused. Check outbound spam, then request removal.
alert.customer: Outbound mail to some providers may be refused for a while. We are working on it.

warn.not_relay_domain: {{domain}} is not a relay domain in Mailfilter yet, so Mailfilter would refuse its mail. Add the domain under Domains first.
warn.mx_leaves_mailfilter: {{domain}} is live on Mailfilter, but this list no longer points to Mailfilter. Mail will bypass the filter.
warn.dnssec_off_host: The zone of the Mailfilter host name is not signed with DNSSEC, so senders ignore this record until DNSSEC is on.

mxe.title: MX records in Cloudflare
mxe.help: Change where mail for this domain is delivered. Use "Only Mailfilter" to send all mail through {{host}}, or keep the old server as a backup with a higher number (lower number = tried first).
mxe.no_cloudflare: Connect Cloudflare on the Cloudflare tab to change the MX records of {{domain}} from here.
mxe.no_zone: {{domain}} is not in your Cloudflare account, so its MX records cannot be changed from here.
mxe.not_managed: {{domain}} is not a relay domain in Mailfilter. Mail sent to Mailfilter for this domain would be refused.

tls.help: These records make sure mail to your domains is always sent encrypted, so nobody on the way can force an unencrypted connection.
tls.sts_help: Tells senders that mail for this domain must be delivered over a verified TLS connection to the listed servers. Mailfilter serves the policy itself on mta-sts.<domain> and gets a certificate for it automatically. Start in test mode and switch to enforce once the MX points to {{host}}.
tls.mode_testing_help: Senders report problems (TLS-RPT) but still deliver.
tls.mode_enforce_help: Senders only deliver over a verified encrypted connection to the listed MX servers.
tls.mode_none_help: Use this to switch MTA-STS off: senders forget the policy.
tls.mx_hint: Every MX of the domain must be listed. *.example.com covers one level.
tls.rpt_help: Senders send a daily report about failed encrypted connections to this address. Useful together with MTA-STS in test mode.
tls.dane_help: A TLSA record with the fingerprint of the key of {{host}}. Senders that support DANE then only deliver encrypted to exactly this server. It only works when DNSSEC is on.
tls.dnssec_how: Turn on DNSSEC in Cloudflare: open the domain, go to DNS > Settings and click Enable DNSSEC. If the domain is not registered with Cloudflare, add the DS record that Cloudflare shows at your registrar.

gateway.apply_failed: Not saved: the mail server check "{{step}}" failed, so nothing was changed.
gateway.applied: Saved and active on the mail server
gateway.last_ok: Mail server configuration is up to date (last change {{at}}).
gateway.last_failed: The last change on {{at}} was refused by the mail server; the previous configuration is still active.
gateway.never_applied: The configuration has not been written from the web interface yet.

domains.title: Domains
domains.sub: Domains the Mailfilter accepts mail for, and the mail server that receives the clean mail.
domains.sub_customer: Your domains and where their mail is delivered.
domains.empty: No domains yet. Add the first domain to start filtering.
domains.name: Domain
domains.not_configured_hint: This domain exists for users, but mail for it is not accepted yet. Enter its mail server to start.
domains.destinations_hint: Clean mail goes to the main server; backup servers are used when it cannot be reached.
domains.mx_hint: Look up the MX records of this host name instead of connecting to it directly.
domains.tls_hint: Required: never deliver without TLS. Verified: also check the certificate.
domains.verify_hint: Ask the mail server before accepting a message, so mail for unknown addresses is refused at the door (no backscatter).
domains.concurrency_hint: How many messages are delivered at the same time. Empty: default.
domains.rate_delay_hint: For mail servers that cannot keep up. Delivers one message at a time.
domains.outbound_hint: Mail sent out from this domain via the Mailfilter. Empty: the default from Throttling.
domains.enabled: Accept and deliver mail for this domain
domains.delete_confirm: Delete {{name}}? Mail for this domain is refused from then on.
domains.tls_sub: Require TLS for specific receiving domains
domains.tls_empty: No rules; encryption is used when available.

relay.title: Relay access
relay.sub: Servers (for example web servers) that may send mail out through the Mailfilter. Their mail is still checked for spam and viruses.
relay.sub_customer: Your servers that may send mail out through the Mailfilter.
relay.hint: Use one IP address for one server, or a network such as 203.0.113.0/28. IPv4 and IPv6 both work.
relay.confirm_broad: Yes, this large network is really ours
relay.ports_sub: Extra ports next to 587 and 465, e.g. for old software

throttling.title: Throttling
throttling.sub: Limits for mail going out through the Mailfilter, so one hacked web server or account cannot send thousands of spam messages.
throttling.defaults_sub: Apply unless a domain has its own limit
throttling.relay_ip_per_minute_hint: Messages one relay IP may send per minute.
throttling.relay_ip_per_hour_hint: Messages one relay IP may send per hour.
throttling.domain_per_hour_hint: Set a different limit per domain under Domains.
throttling.domain_per_day_hint: Set a different limit per domain under Domains.
throttling.user_per_hour_hint: Messages one SMTP login may send per hour.
throttling.concurrency_hint: Default for each domain's own delivery queue.
throttling.destinations_sub: Big providers block senders that go too fast
throttling.domain_limits_hint: Limits for your own domains are set per domain under Domains.

jobs.reconnecting: The web interface is restarting. This page reconnects by itself.
jobs.done_update: Update finished. The page reloads in a moment.
jobs.done_restore: Restore finished. Everything is running again.
jobs.failed_update: Update failed. The previous version was put back.

steps.backup_files: Saving files (settings, DKIM keys, certificates, quarantine)
steps.restore_safety: Making a safety backup of the current state
steps.update_rollback: Update failed, putting the previous version back

backups.title: Backups
backups.sub: Local backups of all settings, DKIM keys, certificates, quarantine, the database and the spam filter's learning data.
backups.empty: No backups yet. The first one is made tonight, or press Full backup now.
backups.verify: Check that the backup is complete
backups.delete: Delete this full backup and its incrementals
backups.delete_confirm: Delete the full backup of {{when}} and all incremental backups that build on it?
backups.nightly_d: Every night; a full backup every {{days}} days, incremental in between.
backups.keep_d: Older ones are removed together with their incrementals.
backups.comp_files_d: settings, lists, passwords, DKIM keys, certificates, quarantined mail
backups.remote_later: Copying backups to FTP, FTPS or SCP comes in a later version.
backups.restore_warn: Restoring replaces the current settings and data with those from this backup. Mail services stop for a moment; incoming mail waits at the sender and is delivered afterwards.
backups.restore_chain_one: This incremental backup builds on the full backup and 1 earlier step; all are replayed in order.
backups.restore_chain_other: This incremental backup builds on the full backup and {{count}} earlier steps; all are replayed in order.
backups.safety: Make a safety backup of the current state first (recommended)

smtp.title: E-mail sending
smtp.sub: How Mailfilter sends its own messages: alerts, quarantine reports, password notices and backup reports.
smtp.mode_local_d: Uses the gateway's own Postfix. Messages are DKIM-signed like all other mail. Recommended.
smtp.mode_smtp_d: For example Microsoft 365, Google Workspace or your own mail server.
smtp.username_d: Leave empty if the server does not need a login.
smtp.password_keep: A password is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
smtp.insecure: Without encryption or certificate check, passwords and mail can be read or changed on the way.
smtp.test_d: Uses the settings in the form, also before saving.
smtp.modern_tls: TLS 1.2 or newer, with certificate checks, through STARTTLS or direct TLS
smtp.modern_auth: SMTP AUTH; the password is stored encrypted
smtp.modern_headers: Date, Message-ID and Auto-Submitted headers, so autoresponders do not reply
smtp.modern_local: Default route through the gateway itself, with DKIM signing

pmg.title: Import from Proxmox Mail Gateway
pmg.sub: Take over domains, relay access, allow and block lists and DKIM from your PMG. You see everything first and choose what to import.
pmg.how1: Open the PMG web interface and go to Administration → Backup/Restore.
pmg.drop: Drop the backup file here or click to choose

help.domains: Domains Mailfilter accepts mail for, with the server mail is delivered to.
help.relay_networks: IP addresses and networks that may send mail out through Mailfilter (PMG: Trusted Networks).
help.address_routes: Single addresses or other domains that go to their own server.
help.tls_policies: Destinations that require an encrypted connection.
help.lists: Senders that are always let through (allow) or always refused (block).
help.dkim: PMG's DKIM key. Taking it over keeps the DKIM records in your DNS valid.
help.rules: PMG filter rules are not converted. Mailfilter does the standard ones itself; check the others and rebuild them if you still need them.
help.settings: Settings from PMG, for reference. Set them under Settings where you want the same values.

pmg.confirm: Import {{count}} items into this Mailfilter? Postfix and Rspamd are checked before anything goes live.
pmg.safe: Everything is checked first; if a check fails, nothing is changed.
pmg.failed: Import not done, nothing was changed

holds.why_spam: {{spam}} of {{total}} messages in {{minutes}} minutes were spam
holds.held_count_one: {{count}} message is on hold, nothing has been lost or sent.
holds.held_count_other: {{count}} messages are on hold, nothing has been lost or sent.
holds.ask_admin: Ask your administrator to release it
holds.release_text: Only do this once the website, server or mailbox is safe again (password changed, hole fixed). New mail goes out normally again. What should happen to the mail that was held?
holds.pause_confirm: Pause {{value}}? Its mail is kept on hold until you release it.

protection.title: Automatic protection
protection.sub: Every minute Mailfilter checks the outgoing mail of each sending server and SMTP account. A sender that suddenly sends spam or far more mail than usual (a hacked website or mailbox) is paused: its mail is kept on hold, administrators get an e-mail, and you release it under Relay access.
protection.enabled_hint: Off: nothing is paused automatically (you can still pause by hand).
protection.window_minutes_hint: How many minutes of mail are checked each time.
protection.spam_min: Spam: at least this many messages
protection.spam_min_hint: A few spam messages are normal; a hacked sender sends many.
protection.spam_percent_hint: And at least this share of all its mail must be spam.
protection.volume_min: Volume: at least this many messages
protection.volume_min_hint: Small senders are never paused for volume.
protection.volume_factor_hint: Compared with the average of the last 7 days.
protection.quiet_hours_hint: So a sender you just released is not paused again straight away.
protection.exempt_hint: IP addresses or SMTP accounts, one per line.
protection.notify_hint: Extra e-mail addresses, one per line. Administrators always get the alert.
